text: The Sermon of Fadak — The Complete Continuous Text
Of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her)
Delivered in the Noble Prophetic Mosque in Medina the Illuminated, after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) and the usurpation of Fadak and the caliphate.

Relied-upon sources: **al-Ihtijaj of al-Tabrisi (vol. 1, pp. 131–149)**, **Bihar al-Anwar of Allama al-Majlisi (vol. 29, pp. 215–335)**, **Kashf al-Ghumma of al-Irbili**, **Dala'il al-Imama of al-Tabari al-Shi'i**, **Balaghat al-Nisa' of Ibn Tayfur**.

---
Introduction of the Narration (The Manner of the Going Forth of al-Zahra, Peace Be Upon Her, to the Mosque)

Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated, with his chain of transmission from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that when Abu Bakr and Umar resolved together upon withholding Fadak from Fatima (peace be upon her), and that reached her, she wound her head-covering (khimar) upon her head, and wrapped herself in her outer garment (jilbab). She came forward in a small company of her attendants and the women of her people, treading upon her trailing hems. Her gait did not fall short [in anything] of the gait of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family).

So it was until she entered upon Abu Bakr while he was in a throng of the Emigrants and the Helpers and others. Then a sheet was hung before her, and she sat down. Then she moaned a moan at which the people burst into weeping, so the assembly shook.

Then she waited a little while, until, when the sobbing of the people had subsided and their surge had calmed, she opened the speech with the praise of Allah, and the laudation of Him, and the blessing upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). So the people returned to their weeping. Then when they held back, she returned to her speech, and she said (peace be upon her):

---
The Text of the Noble Sermon
In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.
Praise be to Allah for what He bestowed, and to Him is thanks for what He inspired,
and laudation for what He sent ahead: of the all-embracing bounties that He originated,
and the amplitude of favors that He conferred, and the completeness of benefactions that He granted in succession;
whose number is too abundant for enumeration, and whose extent is too remote for requital,
and whose perpetuity is beyond comprehension. And He summoned them to seek their increase through thanks, for their continuity,
and He sought praise from the creatures by lavishing them, and He followed up with the summons to their likes.
And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, no partner has He: a word whose interpretation He made sincerity,
and whose bond He lodged within the hearts, and whose intelligible [meaning] He illuminated in reflection. [He is] the One whose being seen is impossible for the eyes,
and whose description [is impossible] for the tongues, and whose modality [is impossible] for the imaginations.
He originated the things not from anything that was before them, and He brought them into being without the following of examples that He imitated.
He formed them by His power and brought them forth by His will, without any need from Him for their formation,
nor any benefit for Him in their shaping,
except as an establishing of His wisdom, and an alerting to His obedience, and a manifesting of His power, and a subjecting of His creation to worship,
and a strengthening of His call. Then He placed the reward upon His obedience, and He laid the punishment upon His disobedience,
as a driving away of His servants from His vengeance, and a herding of them to His Garden.
And I bear witness that my father Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. He chose him before He sent him,
and He named him before He elected him, and He selected him before He raised him [as messenger], when the creatures were hidden in the unseen,
and guarded by the veil of terrors, and joined to the utmost limit of nonexistence: out of knowledge from Allah, the Exalted, of the outcomes of the affairs,
and encompassment of the events of the ages, and cognizance of the places where the affairs befall.
Allah raised him as a completion of His command, and a resolve upon the execution of His judgment,
and an implementation of the decrees of His mercy. So he saw the nations as sects in their religions,
clinging in devotion to their fires, worshipping their idols, denying Allah despite their recognition [of Him].
So Allah illuminated through my father Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family) their darknesses, and removed from the hearts their obscurities,
and cleared from the eyes their coverings. And he stood among the people with guidance, so he rescued them from misguidance,
and gave them sight out of blindness, and guided them to the upright religion, and called them to the straight path.
Then Allah took him to Himself, a taking of compassion and choice, and of desire and preference. So Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family) is, from the toil of this abode, in rest.
He has been surrounded by the righteous angels, and the good pleasure of the All-forgiving Lord, and the neighborhood of the All-compelling King.
May Allah bless my father, His Prophet, and His trusted one, and His choice one from the creation, and His elect; and peace be upon him, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
Then she turned to the people of the assembly and said:
You, O servants of Allah, are the appointed standards of His command and His prohibition, and the bearers of His religion and His revelation, and the trustees of Allah over yourselves,
and His conveyers to the nations. A guarantor of a right of His is among you, and a covenant that He sent ahead to you, and a remnant that He left as successor over you:
the speaking Book of Allah, and the truthful Qur'an, and the radiant light, and the gleaming illumination;
its insights evident, its secrets unveiled, its outward [meanings] manifest, its adherents enviable on account of it;
its following leading to the good pleasure, its hearing conducting to salvation. By it are attained the illuminated proofs of Allah,
and His expounded binding ordinances, and His warned-against prohibitions, and His clarifying evidences, and His sufficient demonstrations,
and His recommended virtues, and His bestowed concessions, and His prescribed laws.
So Allah made faith a purification for you from polytheism, and prayer a keeping of you clear of pride,
and the zakat a purification for the soul and a growth in sustenance, and fasting an establishing of sincerity,
and the hajj a raising up of the religion, and justice a harmonizing of the hearts,
and obedience to us an order for the religious community, and our Imamate a security against division,
and jihad a might for Islam, and patience an aid toward the deserving of the reward,
and the enjoining of what is right a welfare for the public, and dutifulness to the parents a protection from wrath,
and the joining of the ties of kinship a prolonging of the lifespan and a multiplying of the number, and retaliation (qisas) a sparing of blood,
and the fulfillment of the vow an exposing [of oneself] to forgiveness, and the giving in full of the measures and the weights an altering of diminution,
and the prohibition of the drinking of wine a keeping clear of defilement, and the avoidance of slanderous accusation a veil from the curse,
and the abandonment of theft a necessitating of chaste restraint. And Allah forbade polytheism as a sincerity to Him in Lordship.
So fear Allah with the fear due to Him, and do not die except while you are Muslims,
and obey Allah in what He commanded you and what He forbade you, for indeed only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.
Then she said:
O people! Know that I am Fatima, and my father is Muhammad. I say [it] returning and beginning,
and I do not say what I say in error, nor do I do what I do in excess.
There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what distresses you; full of concern over you; to the believers compassionate, merciful.
So if you trace his lineage and know him, you will find him my father, to the exclusion of your women,
and the brother of the son of my paternal uncle, to the exclusion of your men. And how excellent indeed is he to whom [lineage] is traced (may Allah bless him and his family)!
So he conveyed the message, proclaiming openly the warning, turning aside from the pathway of the polytheists,
striking their mid-backs, seizing their throats, calling to the way of his Lord with wisdom and goodly exhortation,
breaking the idols and casting down the heads, until the host was routed and they turned the back;
until the night split apart from its morning, and the truth unveiled its pure essence,
and the leader of the religion spoke, and the bellowing foam-sacs of the satans fell dumb, and the rabble of hypocrisy perished,
and the knots of disbelief and schism came undone,
and you uttered the word of sincerity among a small band of the white [-faced], the lean [-bellied] ones.
And you were upon the brink of a pit of the Fire: the [watered] draught of the drinker,
and the opportunity of the covetous, and the firebrand of the hasty, and the treading-place of the feet. You were drinking the fouled water,
and feeding on dried strips of hide, abased, driven off in scorn, fearing that the people would snatch you away from around you.
So Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, rescued you through Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family), after the little [calamity] and the [great] one,
and after he was afflicted with the dauntless warriors among men, and the wolves of the Arabs, and the insolent rebels of the People of the Book.
Whenever they kindled a fire for war, Allah extinguished it. Or [whenever] the horn of Satan emerged,
or a gaping maw of the polytheists opened wide, he hurled his brother into its throat. And he would not turn back until he trod its wing with the hollow of his foot,
and quenched its flame with his sword: toil-worn in the Self of Allah, striving in the affair of Allah, near to the Messenger of Allah,
a master among the friends of Allah, with garment tucked up [in readiness], sincerely counseling, earnest, laboring. The blame of a blamer does not take hold of him in [the way of] Allah.
And you were in comfort of living, reposeful, enjoying, secure,
awaiting for us the turns of misfortune, and watching expectantly for the news, and recoiling at the encounter, and fleeing from the fighting.
Then when Allah chose for His Prophet the abode of His prophets and the refuge of His elect ones,

there appeared among you the thorn of hypocrisy. And the outer garment of the religion became worn out, and the silenced one of the misguided spoke, and the obscure one of the lowliest rose to prominence,
and the stallion of the falsifiers bellowed, and he swaggered in your open grounds. And Satan put forth his head from his hiding-place, calling aloud to you,
and he found you responsive to his call, and regardful of the deception in him. Then he roused you, and he found you light [to move],
and he inflamed you, and he found you wrathful. So you branded other than your camels, and you came to water at other than your watering place.
This, while the covenant was recent, and the gash wide, and the wound not yet healed,
and the Messenger not yet entombed! Hastening, [as] you alleged, out of fear of sedition (fitnah):
surely into sedition they have fallen, and indeed Hell is encompassing the disbelievers.
So how far [that is] from you! And how [is it] with you? And how are you turned away, while the Book of Allah is in your midst? Its matters are manifest,
and its rulings radiant, and its signposts dazzling, and its restraints evident, and its commands clear.
And you have left it behind your backs! Is it turning away from it in aversion that you desire? Or by other than it do you judge?
Wretched for the wrongdoers is the exchange! And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it shall never be accepted from him, and he in the Hereafter is among the losers.
Then you did not tarry except the while that its shying might quieten and its leading-rein become easy. Then you began to strike fire for its blaze,
and to stir up its ember, and to respond to the calling aloud of Satan the misleader, and [to] the extinguishing of the lights of the manifest religion,
and the neglecting of the practices (sunan) of the elect Prophet. You conceal a sipping within a skimming of the froth, and you walk against his family and his children in the covert and the thicket.
And we endure from you the like of the slashing of knives, and the piercing of the spearhead in the entrails.
And you now allege that there is no inheritance for us! Is it then the judgment of the [Age of] Ignorance (Jahiliyyah) that you seek?
And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain? Do you not then know?
Yes indeed! It has become manifest to you like the forenoon sun that I am his daughter.
O Muslims! Am I to be overcome with regard to my inheritance?
O son of Abu Quhafa! Is it in the Book of Allah that you inherit from your father and I do not inherit from my father?
You have certainly brought a monstrous thing! Is it then deliberately that you have abandoned the Book of Allah and cast it behind your backs, when He says: “And Sulayman inherited from Dawud”;
and He said, in what He related of the account of Zakariyya, when he said: “So grant me from Yourself an heir (wali) who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub”;
and He said: “And the possessors of blood relationship, some of them are nearer to others in the Book of Allah”;
and He said: “Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the share of the two females”;
and He said: “If he leaves wealth, the bequest is for the parents and the near relatives according to what is right, a duty upon the God-fearing.”

And you alleged that there is no favored share for me, and that I do not inherit from my father, and that there is no kinship between us! Did Allah then single you out with a verse from which He excluded my father?
Or do you say: the people of two religious communities do not inherit from each other?
Am I and my father not of the people of one religious community?
Or are you more knowing of the particular of the Qur'an and its general than my father and the son of my paternal uncle?
So here, take it, nose-haltered and saddled; it will meet you on the day of your mustering.
For excellent is the Judge, Allah; and the guarantor, Muhammad; and the appointed tryst, the Resurrection. And at the Hour the falsifiers will lose,
and it will not benefit you when you regret. And for every tiding is an appointed settling,
and you shall surely come to know to whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend an abiding punishment.
Then she cast her glance toward the Helpers (Ansar), and said:
O company of noble valor, and upper arms of the religious community, and nurturers of Islam! What is this flagging in regard to my right, and this drowsiness toward my grievance?
Was not the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), my father, wont to say: “A man is safeguarded in his children”?
How swiftly you have innovated! And how hasty [is this], possessor of melted fat! And you have capacity for what I attempt, and strength for what I seek and pursue.
Do you say: Muhammad has died?
Then [it is] a momentous calamity whose weakness has widened, and whose rent has flowed wide [as a river], and whose mended seam has torn open.
And the earth was darkened for his absence,
and the sun and the moon were eclipsed, and the stars were scattered for his calamity,
and the hopes struck barren rock, and the mountains were humbled, and the sanctuary was squandered, and the sanctity was removed at his death.
So that, by Allah, is the greatest affliction and the mightiest calamity. There is no affliction the like of it,
nor any swift disaster [like it]. The Book of Allah, majestic is His praise, proclaimed it in your courtyards,
and in your evening and your morning, calling aloud in your courtyards with a calling aloud, and an outcrying, and a recitation, and melodies.
And before him, [it is] what befell the prophets of Allah and His messengers: a decisive judgment and an inevitable decree.

“And Muhammad is not but a messenger; the messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is slain, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels will never harm Allah in anything, and Allah will recompense the grateful.”
Come now, O sons of Qaylah! Am I to be defrauded of the heritage of my father while you are within sight of me and hearing, and [within] a gathering-place and an assembly?
The call clothes you, and the awareness encompasses you. And you are possessors of number and equipment and instrument and strength, and with you are the weapons and the shield.
The call reaches you, yet you do not answer; and the outcry comes to you, yet you do not succor. And you are described by combat,
known for goodness and righteousness, and the elite that was selected, and the choice ones that were chosen for us, the People of the House.

You fought the Arabs, and you bore the toil and the fatigue, and you butted against the nations, and you combated the dauntless warriors. We did not cease, nor did you cease; we commanding you and you complying,
until, when the mill of Islam revolved through us, and the milk of the days flowed abundantly, and the snorting pride of polytheism was humbled, and the boiling of the lie subsided,
and the fires of disbelief died down, and the call of tumult grew calm, and the order of the religion became well-arranged: then whither have you swerved after the clarification,
and concealed after the proclamation, and recoiled after the advance, and associated [partners] after the faith?
Wretchedness to a people who broke their oaths after their covenant, and resolved upon the expulsion of the Messenger, and they began [against] you the first time!
Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers.
Behold! I do see that you have clung to ease, and you have put far away him who is more entitled to the extending and the grasping,
and you have secluded yourselves with repose, and you have escaped from the spaciousness into the straitness. So you have spat out what you had taken in,
and you have vomited that which you had swallowed with ease. So if you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth altogether, then indeed Allah is surely Self-sufficient, Praiseworthy.
Behold! I have said what I have said, this, with knowledge on my part of the forsaking that has permeated you,

and the treachery that your hearts have taken as an inner garment. But it is the overflow of the soul, and the exhalation of rage, and the giving way of the spear-shaft, and the unburdening of the breast, and the presenting in advance of the proof.
[Then Abu Bakr said:] O daughter of the Messenger of Allah! Your father was indeed, toward the believers, tender, generous, compassionate, merciful,
and upon the disbelievers a painful punishment and a tremendous chastisement.
If we trace his lineage, we find him your father, to the exclusion of the women,
and the brother of your intimate [consort], to the exclusion of the close friends.
He preferred him over every close friend, and he assisted him in every momentous affair.
None loves you except a felicitous one, and none hates you except a wretched one, far removed.
For you are the progeny ('itrah) of the Messenger of Allah, the pure ones, the choice ones, the nobly selected;
upon the good [you are] our guides, and to the Garden our pathways.
And you, O choice one of the women and daughter of the best of the prophets,
are truthful in your saying, foremost in the abundance of your intellect,
not turned back from your right, nor barred from your truthfulness.
By Allah, I did not go beyond the view of the Messenger of Allah, nor did I act except by his permission; and the scout does not lie to his people.
And indeed I call Allah to witness, and sufficient is He as a witness,
that I heard the Messenger of Allah saying:

“We, the companies of the prophets, do not bequeath gold nor silver, nor a house nor landed estate; and we only bequeath the Book and wisdom and knowledge and prophethood. And whatever we had of a means of sustenance (tu'mah), then it is for the guardian of the affair after us to judge concerning it by his judgment.”
And we have placed what you sought into the horses and the weapons,
with which the Muslims fight and wage jihad against the disbelievers,
and battle the insolent rebels, the wicked. And that is by the consensus of the Muslims.
I was not alone in it by myself, nor did I act despotically in what the view was with me.
And this is my state and my wealth: it is for you and before your hands. It is not withdrawn from you, nor do we hoard [it] away from you.
And indeed you, and you are the mistress of the community of your father and the goodly tree for your sons: what is yours of your excellence is not repelled,
nor is [anything] lowered in your branch and your root. Your judgment is effective in what my two hands possess.
So do you deem that I should oppose your father (may Allah bless him and his family and grant peace) in that?
Then she said: Glory be to Allah! My father, the Messenger of Allah, was not one to turn away from the Book of Allah, nor one to oppose its rulings.
Rather, he used to follow its track, and trail its chapters.
Do you then join to the treachery a pretexting against him with falsehood?
And this, after his passing, is similar to what was sought against him of ruinous plots in his lifetime. This is the Book of Allah, a just arbiter and a decisive speaker.
It says: “He will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub,” and it says: “And Sulayman inherited from Dawud.”
He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear, in what He distributed of the portions, and legislated of the obligatory shares and the inheritance,
and permitted of the share of the males and the females, that by which He removed the pretext of the falsifiers, and did away with conjecture and doubts among those remaining [afterward].
Nay! Rather, your souls have made a matter seem fair to you. So [mine is] a beautiful patience, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.

Then Abu Bakr said: Allah has spoken the truth, and His Messenger, and his daughter has spoken the truth: the mine of wisdom, and the homeland of guidance and mercy, and the pillar of the religion, and the very essence of the proof. I do not deem your correctness remote, nor do I deny your address.

These Muslims are between me and you. They invested me with what I have been invested with, and by an agreement from them I took what I took: not being obstinate, nor despotic, nor appropriating exclusively. And they are witnesses to that.
Then Fatima (peace be upon her) turned to the women, and said: O companies of the Muslims, who hasten to the saying of falsehood, who close their eyes upon the ugly, losing deed!
Do you not then ponder the Qur'an, or are there upon hearts their locks?
Nay! Rather, what you have done ill of your deeds has rusted over your hearts,
so it has seized your hearing and your sight. And wretched indeed is what you have interpreted, and evil is what you have counseled, and wicked is what you have taken in exchange!
You shall surely find, by Allah, its burden heavy and its aftermath baneful, when the cover is removed for you, and what is behind it, the adversity, becomes plain,

and there appears to you from your Lord what you had not been reckoning; and there and then the falsifiers lose.

---
What Is After the Sermon: At the Grave of the Messenger of Allah (May Allah Bless Him and His Family)
Then she (peace be upon her) turned toward the grave of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and said:
There have been, after you, tidings and tangled troubles ... had you been witness to them, the calamities would not have multiplied.
Indeed we have lost you as the earth loses its heavy rain ... and your people have fallen into disorder, so witness them and do not be absent.
So would that, before you, death had befallen us ... when your death was announced and the heaped mounds intervened before you.
Men have scowled at us, and we have been held in contempt ... since you became absent from us, and all the good they have usurped.
The one who took charge of the wronging of our protector shall come to know ... on the Day of Resurrection whither I was returning.
Men disclosed to us the purport of their breasts ... when you were lost, and all the inheritance they have usurped.
And every people have kinship and standing ... with the God, and for the nearest ones there is nearness.

Indeed we have been afflicted with that with which [no] possessors of grief have been afflicted ... among creation, neither non-Arabs nor Arabs.

---
The Dialogue of Abu Bakr with al-Zahra (Peace Be Upon Her) and Her Answer to Him
**The answer of Abu Bakr:**
Then Abu Bakr answered her and said:

“O daughter of the Messenger of Allah, your father was indeed, toward the believers, tender, generous, compassionate, merciful, and upon the disbelievers a painful punishment and a tremendous chastisement. If we trace his lineage, we find him your father, to the exclusion of the women, and the brother of the son of your paternal uncle, to the exclusion of the men. He preferred him over every close friend, and he assisted him in every momentous affair. None loves you except a felicitous one, and none hates you except a wretched one.

For you are the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), the pure ones, and the choice ones, the nobly selected; upon the good [you are] our guides, and to the Garden our pathways. And you, O choice one of the women and daughter of the best of the prophets, are truthful in your saying, foremost in the abundance of your intellect, not turned back from your right, nor barred from your truthfulness.

By Allah, I did not go beyond the view of the Messenger of Allah, nor did I act except by his permission; and indeed the scout does not lie to his people. And indeed I call Allah to witness, and sufficient is He as a witness, that I heard the Messenger of Allah saying: ‘We, the companies of the prophets, do not bequeath gold nor silver, nor a house nor landed estate; and we only bequeath the Book and wisdom and knowledge and prophethood. And whatever we had of a means of sustenance, then it is for the guardian of the affair after us to judge concerning it by his judgment.’

And we have placed what you sought into the horses and the weapons, with which the Muslims fight, and wage jihad against the disbelievers, and battle the insolent rebels, the wicked. And that is by a consensus of the Muslims. I was not alone in it by myself, nor did I act despotically in that wherein was my view.

And this is my state and my wealth: it is for you and before your hands. It is not withdrawn from you, nor is it hoarded away from you. And indeed you are the mistress of the community of your father, and the goodly tree for your sons. We do not repel what is yours of your excellence, nor is [anything] lowered in your root and your branch. Your judgment is effective in what my two hands possess. So do you deem that I should oppose your father in that?”
**The reply of the Lady Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her):**
Then she (peace be upon her) said:

“Glory be to Allah! The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) was not one to turn away from the Book of Allah, nor one to oppose its rulings. Rather, he used to follow its track, and trail its chapters. Do you then join to the treachery a pretexting against him with falsehood?! And this, after his passing, is similar to what was sought against him of ruinous plots in his lifetime!

This is the Book of Allah, a just arbiter and a decisive speaker. It says: ﴿He will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, and it says: ﴿And Sulayman inherited from Dawud﴾. So He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear, in what He apportioned thereon of the portions, and legislated of the obligatory shares and the inheritance, and permitted of the share of the males and the females, that by which He removed the pretext of the falsifiers, and did away with conjecture and doubts among those remaining [afterward]. Nay! ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter seem fair to you; so [mine is] a beautiful patience, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾.”

---
Her Dialogue with the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (Peace Be Upon Him), upon Her Return to the House

Then she (peace be upon her) turned back, while the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was awaiting her return to him and looking out for her appearing before him. Then when the house had settled with her, she said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him):

“O son of Abu Talib, you have wrapped yourself in the wrapping of the fetus, and you have sat in the chamber of the suspect! You broke the foremost pinion of the falcon, then the feathers of the unarmed betrayed you! This is the son of Abu Quhafa, wresting from me the gift (nihlah) of my father and the bare subsistence of my two sons!

He has indeed been open against me in my dispute, and I found him most obstinate in [opposing] my speech, until Qaylah withheld from me her help, and the Emigrants their bond, and the community lowered its gaze away from me. So there is no defender and no preventer. I went out restraining [my rage], and I returned humbled.

You abased your cheek the day you squandered your edge! You used to prey upon the wolves, and [now] you have spread the dust for a bed! You did not restrain a speaker, nor did you avail anything of use, and there is no choice for me. Would that I had died before my lowliness and short of my abasement!

My excuser is Allah, from you as an assailant, and from you as a protector! Woe is me at every sunrise, woe is me at every sunset! The support has died, and the upper arm has weakened. My complaint is to my father, and my appeal for redress is to my Lord. O Allah, You are stronger in power and might, and sharper in force and exemplary punishment.”
Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to her:

“No woe is for you; rather, the woe is for the one who hates you. Restrain yourself from your grief, O daughter of the Elect and remnant of prophethood, for I have not slackened from my religion, nor have I missed what was within my power. So if you desire the bare subsistence, then your sustenance is guaranteed, and your surety is trustworthy; and what has been prepared for you is better than what has been cut off from you. So reckon [your recompense] with Allah.”
Then she (peace be upon her) said: “Allah suffices me,” and she held back.
The Sermon of Fadak — The Complete Text
By the Lady of the Women of the Worlds, Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her)

Delivered in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina after the death of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), and after the seizure of Fadak and of the caliphate. Fadak was a fertile farming estate north of Medina that the Prophet had given to her. The caliphate is the leadership of the Muslim community.

Sources relied upon: **al-Ihtijaj by al-Tabarsi (vol. 1, pp. 131–149)**, **Bihar al-Anwar by Allama al-Majlisi (vol. 29, pp. 215–335)**, **Kashf al-Ghumma by al-Irbili**, **Dala'il al-Imama by al-Tabari al-Shi'i**, **Balaghat al-Nisa' by Ibn Tayfur**.

---
Introduction to the Account (How al-Zahra, Peace Be Upon Her, Went Out to the Mosque)

Abdullah ibn al-Hasan related this through his chain of transmission from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

Abu Bakr and Umar agreed together to withhold Fadak from Fatima (peace be upon her). Abu Bakr had taken power as caliph after the Prophet's death. When the news reached her, she wound her head-covering about her head and wrapped herself in her outer cloak. She set out with a small group of her attendants and the women of her kin. Her garments were so long that she trod on their hems. Her walk differed in no way from the walk of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family).

She came in to Abu Bakr, who was sitting among a crowd of others. These included the Emigrants (Muslims who had left Mecca with the Prophet) and the Helpers (the Ansar, Muslims of Medina who had sheltered and supported him). A curtain was hung to screen her, and she sat down behind it. Then she let out a moan of grief so deep that the people broke into weeping, and the whole gathering was shaken.

She waited a little while, until their sobbing had quieted and their agitation had calmed. Then she opened her speech with praise of God and blessings upon the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family). At this the people began to weep again. When they fell silent, she resumed her speech and said (peace be upon her):

---
The Text of the Noble Sermon
In the name of God, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful.
Praise be to God for the blessings He has given, and thanks be to Him for what He has inspired.
Honour be to Him for all that He gave beforehand: the all-embracing blessings He began with,
the abundant bounties He granted, and the complete favours He conferred.
Their number is too great to be counted, their extent too vast to be repaid,
and their endlessness is beyond understanding. He urged His creatures to seek more of these blessings through gratitude, so that the blessings would continue.
He invited their praise by giving generously. Then He called them again to seek more blessings of the same kind.
I bear witness that there is no god but God, alone, without any partner. He made sincere devotion the true meaning of this statement.
He planted its bond in hearts, and He made its meaning shine in reflective minds. He is the One whom eyes cannot see,
whom tongues cannot describe, and whose nature imagination cannot picture.
He originated all things, not from anything that existed before them. He brought them into being without copying any model.
He formed them by His power and spread them forth by His will. He had no need to create them,
and He gained no benefit for Himself from shaping them.

He did so only:
- to confirm His wisdom,
- to awaken His creatures to obedience,
- to display His power,
- to lead His creatures to worship Him,

- and to give strength to His call.

Then He set reward for obedience to Him and punishment for disobedience.
He did this to drive His servants away from His wrath and gather them toward His Paradise.
I bear witness that my father, Muhammad, is His servant and His Messenger. God chose him before He sent him,
named him before He selected him, and singled him out before He raised him as a prophet. This was at a time when all creatures were still hidden in the unseen.
They were screened behind veils of dread and bound to the very edge of non-existence. For God Most High knew how all matters would end,
encompassed the events of all the ages, and knew where every destined thing would fall.
God sent him to complete His plan, to carry out His judgment with resolve,
and to put into effect what His mercy had decreed. He found the nations divided in their religions.
Some were devoted to their sacred fires and some worshipped their idols, all denying God even though they knew of Him.
So through my father Muhammad (may God bless him and his family), God lit up their darkness. He removed the confusion from their hearts
and cleared the clouds from their eyes. My father stood among the people with guidance. He rescued them from error
and gave them sight in place of blindness. He guided them to the upright religion and called them to the straight path.

Then God took him to Himself, a taking in kindness and by choice, out of longing for him and preference for him. So Muhammad (may God bless him and his family) is now at rest from the toil of this world.
He is surrounded by the righteous angels, by the good pleasure of the All-Forgiving Lord, and by nearness to the Almighty King.
May God bless my father: His Prophet, His trusted one, His choice from among all creation, and His pure friend. Peace be upon him, and the mercy of God and His blessings.
Then she turned to the people in the assembly and said:
You, servants of God, are the ones appointed to uphold His commands and prohibitions. You are the bearers of His religion and His revelation, God's trustees over your own selves,

and His messengers to the other nations.

Among you is a rightful authority that belongs to Him, a covenant He set before you in advance, and a legacy He left behind to stand over you.
It is the speaking Book of God, the truthful Quran, the radiant light, the shining brilliance.
Its insights are clear, its secrets are laid open, and its outward meanings are plain. Its followers are envied for it.

Following it leads to God's good pleasure, and listening to it leads to salvation. Through it are reached:
- God's luminous proofs,

- His explained obligations and the forbidden things He warned against,
- His clear evidences and His sufficient demonstrations,

- His recommended virtues and the permissions He granted,
- and the laws He prescribed.
So God made faith a way to purify you from idolatry, and prayer a way to free you from pride.
He made the alms-tax (zakat) a purification of the soul and a growth in provision, and fasting a way to make sincerity firm.
He made the pilgrimage (hajj) a way to raise up the religion, and justice a way to bring hearts into harmony.
He made obedience to us [the Prophet's family] the order of the community, and our leadership (the Imamate) a safeguard against division.
He made striving in God's cause (jihad) a glory for Islam, and patience a help in earning reward.
He made enjoining what is right a benefit for the public, and kindness to parents a protection against God's displeasure.
He made keeping ties with relatives a way to lengthen life and increase numbers, and just retaliation for killing a way to spare blood.
He made keeping one's vows a way to become open to forgiveness, and giving full measure and full weight a way to end cheating.
He made the ban on drinking wine a way to stay clean of filth, and the avoidance of slanderous accusations of unchastity a screen against God's curse.
He made abstaining from theft a way to ensure integrity. And God forbade setting up partners beside Him, so that He alone would be acknowledged as Lord, in pure devotion.
So “be mindful of God as He truly deserves, and do not die except as people who have submitted to Him” [Quran 3:102].
Obey God in what He has commanded you and in what He has forbidden you. For “among His servants, only those who have knowledge truly stand in awe of God” [Quran 35:28].
Then she said:
O people! Know that I am Fatima, and my father is Muhammad. I say it again as I said it at the beginning.
I do not say what I say in error, and I do not do what I do out of excess.
“There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. It grieves him that you should suffer; he is full of concern for you; and toward the believers he is kind and merciful” [Quran 9:128].
If you trace his lineage and come to know him, you will find that he is my father, and not the father of any of your women.
You will also find that he is the brother of my cousin [Ali], and not the brother of any of your men. How excellent it is to be linked to him, may God bless him and his family!
He delivered the message, openly proclaiming the warning. He turned away from the path of the idol-worshippers,
struck at their backs, and seized them by the throat. He called to the way of his Lord “with wisdom and good counsel” [Quran 16:125].
He smashed the idols and struck down the heads of the arrogant, until their host was routed and they turned and fled.
Then the night split open to reveal its dawn, and the truth appeared in its pure form.
The leader of the religion spoke, and the loud bellowing of the devils fell dumb. The rabble of hypocrisy perished,
and the knots of unbelief and discord came undone.
And you spoke the word of pure devotion, among a small band of people bright of face and lean with hunger.
Before that, you were “on the brink of a pit of fire” [Quran 3:103]. You were a mere gulp for any drinker
and an easy prize for any greedy man. You were a firebrand snatched up by anyone in a hurry, and ground trampled under every foot. You drank foul, muddied water
and fed on strips of dried hide. You were humbled and despised, “afraid that the people around you would snatch you away” [Quran 8:26].
Then God, blessed and exalted, rescued you through Muhammad (may God bless him and his family). This came after troubles small and great.
It came after he had been tried by the fiercest of warriors, the wolves of the Arabs, and the defiant ones among the People of the Book [Jews and Christians].
“Whenever they lit a fire for war, God put it out” [Quran 5:64]. Whenever the horn of Satan showed itself,
or the idol-worshippers opened a gaping mouth, he hurled his brother [Ali] into its throat. Ali would not turn back until he had trampled its wing beneath his foot

and put out its flame with his sword.

Ali wore himself out for God's sake and strove in God's cause. He was close to the Messenger of God
and a master among the friends of God. He was ever ready for action, sincere, earnest, and tireless. Where God was concerned, no one's blame could turn him aside.
Meanwhile you were living in comfort: at ease, enjoying yourselves, and safe.
You waited for misfortune to turn against us and listened eagerly for the news. You drew back when battle came, and you fled from the fighting.
Then God chose for His Prophet the home of His prophets and the refuge of His chosen ones.

At once the thorn of hypocrisy appeared among you, and the robe of religion wore thin. The misguided man who had kept silent found his voice, and the obscure man from among the lowly rose to prominence.

The stallion of the followers of falsehood bellowed and strutted through your courtyards.

Satan raised his head from his hiding place and called out to you.
He found you ready to answer his call and eager for his deception. He urged you to rise, and found you quick to move.
He inflamed you, and found you ready with anger. So you branded camels that were not yours and went down to drink at a watering-place that was not yours [you laid hold of what did not belong to you].
All this happened while the covenant was still recent, the gash still wide, and the wound not yet healed.
The Messenger had not even been buried! You rushed ahead, claiming that you feared civil strife.
“Surely, into strife they have already fallen, and Hell indeed surrounds the unbelievers” [Quran 9:49].
How far this is from you! What has come over you? How have you been turned away from the truth, when the Book of God is right there among you? Its matters are plain
and its rulings shine. Its signposts are dazzling, its warnings are evident, and its commands are clear.
Yet you have thrown it behind your backs. Do you want to turn away from it? Or do you judge by something other than it?

“What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers!” [Quran 18:50]. “Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers” [Quran 3:85].
Then you waited only until its fright had settled and its reins had become easy to handle. [She pictures the seized leadership as a restive camel.] After that you began to fan its blaze
and stir its embers. You answered the call of Satan the misleader. You put out the lights of the clear religion,

and you let the practices of the chosen Prophet fall into neglect.

You pretend only to skim the froth while secretly drinking the milk [you show one purpose and pursue another]. You creep up on his family and his children under cover of thickets and trees.
And we bear what you do to us as one bears the slash of knives and the stab of spearheads in the belly.
And now you claim that we have no inheritance! “Is it the judgment of the Age of Ignorance [the pagan time before Islam] that you seek?
And who is better than God in judgment for a people who have certainty?” [Quran 5:50]. Do you not know?
Yes indeed, it is as clear to you as the midday sun that I am his daughter.
O Muslims! Am I to be overpowered and robbed of my inheritance?
O son of Abu Quhafa [Abu Bakr]! Is it in the Book of God that you inherit from your father, but I do not inherit from mine?

“You have surely come up with a monstrous thing!” [Quran 19:27]. Did you deliberately abandon the Book of God and cast it behind your backs?

For it says: “And Solomon inherited from David” [Quran 27:16].
In telling the story of Zechariah, it relates that he said: “So grant me, from Yourself, an heir who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob” [Quran 19:5–6].
It says: “Blood relatives have the stronger claim to one another in the Book of God” [Quran 8:75].
It says: “God instructs you concerning your children: for the male, a share equal to that of two females” [Quran 4:11].
And it says: “If he leaves wealth, let him make a bequest to parents and nearest relatives in fairness, a duty upon the God-fearing” [Quran 2:180].
Yet you claim that I have no share, that I inherit nothing from my father, and that there is no kinship between us! Did God single you out with a verse from which He excluded my father?
Or do you say, “People of two different religions do not inherit from one another”?
Are my father and I not people of one and the same religion?
Or do you know the specific and the general meanings of the Quran better than my father and my cousin [Ali]?
Then take it, haltered and saddled like a camel ready for its rider! It will meet you on the Day you are raised and gathered.
What an excellent judge God is! Muhammad is the one who will claim our right, and the appointed meeting is the Resurrection. When the Hour comes, the followers of falsehood will lose,
and your regret will be of no use to you then. “For every tiding there is an appointed time” [Quran 6:67],
“and you will come to know who it is that will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom a lasting punishment will descend” [Quran 11:39].
Then she cast her glance toward the Helpers (the Ansar) and said:
O people of noble valour, strong arms of the faith, guardians of Islam! What is this slackness concerning my right, and this drowsiness in the face of the wrong done to me?
Did not the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), my father, say: “A man is honoured through the care shown to his children”?
How quickly you have changed, and how hasty this turn has been! Yet you have the ability to help in what I am striving for, and the strength for what I seek and pursue.
Do you say, “Muhammad has died”?
That is indeed a tremendous blow. Its breach has grown wide, its tear has spread like a flood, and what was once mended has been ripped apart.
The earth went dark at his absence.
The sun and the moon were eclipsed, and the stars were scattered, at the calamity of his loss.
Hopes failed and the mountains were humbled. What was sacred was left unprotected, and all sanctity was swept away at his death.
That, by God, is the greatest disaster and the mightiest affliction. There is no disaster like it
and no sudden calamity to equal it. Yet the Book of God, exalted is His praise, announced it in your very courtyards.
In your evenings and your mornings it called out among you, in loud cry and proclamation, in recitation and in melody.
It told you that what befell God's prophets and messengers before him is a decisive ruling and an inescapable decree:

“Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God in the least, and God will reward the grateful” [Quran 3:144].

Come now, sons of Qayla [the ancestress of the two tribes of Medina who made up the Helpers]! Am I to be robbed of my father's inheritance while you are right here, gathered and assembled, where you can see me and hear me?
The call for help surrounds you, and the knowledge of what is happening reaches you all. You have numbers and equipment, means and strength, and you have weapons and shields.

The call reaches you, yet you do not answer. The cry comes to you, yet you do not come to the rescue.

And you are the ones famed for fighting
and known for goodness and righteousness. You are the elite who were selected, the best who were chosen for us, the People of the House [the Prophet's own family].
You fought the Arabs and bore toil and exhaustion. You locked horns with the nations and battled the fiercest champions. We did not give up, nor did you; we commanded and you obeyed.
So it was until, through us, the mill of Islam began to turn and the milk of the days flowed freely. The snorting pride of idolatry was humbled, and the boiling of falsehood settled.

The fires of unbelief died down, the call to chaos fell quiet, and the order of the religion was firmly established.

How, then, have you strayed after things were made clear?
Why have you concealed the truth after proclaiming it? Why have you drawn back after advancing, and set up partners beside God after believing?
Wretched are “a people who broke their oaths after making their pledge, who resolved to drive out the Messenger, and who attacked you first.
Do you fear them? God has more right to be feared by you, if you are believers” [Quran 9:12–13].
Indeed, I see that you have settled into a life of ease. You have pushed away the one who has the greatest right to govern, to give and to withhold [Ali].
You have withdrawn into comfort and fled from openness into narrowness. You have spat out what you once took in,
and vomited up what you once swallowed so smoothly. “If you are ungrateful, you and everyone on earth together, God is free of all need, worthy of all praise” [Quran 14:8].
Now, I have said all that I have said knowing full well the spirit of desertion that has seeped into you,

and the betrayal your hearts have wrapped themselves in. But this is:
- the overflow of a soul in pain,
- the breathing out of anger,
- the giving way of endurance, as a spear-shaft bends under strain,
- the outpouring of what fills the breast,
- and the setting forth of the proof in advance.

*[Abu Bakr replied:]*

O daughter of the Messenger of God! Your father was indeed tender and generous, kind and merciful to the believers,
and to the unbelievers he was a painful torment and a mighty punishment.
If we trace his lineage, we find that he is your father and not the father of any other woman.
He is also the brother of your husband, and not of any other close companion.
The Prophet preferred him over every close friend, and he aided the Prophet in every great matter.
Only the blessed love you, and only the wretched, far from good, hate you.
You are the pure family of the Messenger of God, the chosen and the select.
You are our guides to what is good and our pathways to Paradise.
And you, best of women and daughter of the best of prophets,
are truthful in what you say and foremost in the fullness of your understanding.
You are not to be turned away from your right, nor barred from your truth.
By God, I have not gone beyond the view of the Messenger of God, nor have I acted except by his leave. The scout does not lie to his own people.
I call God to witness, and God is enough as a witness,
that I heard the Messenger of God say:

“We, the company of prophets, do not leave gold or silver, house or land, as inheritance. We leave as inheritance only the Book, wisdom, knowledge, and prophethood. Whatever means of livelihood we had belongs to the one in authority after us, to decide about it as he judges.”
We have assigned what you are seeking to horses and weapons.
With them the Muslims will fight, wage jihad against the unbelievers,
and battle the defiant evildoers. This was done by the consensus of the Muslims.
I did not act on it alone, nor did I impose my own opinion.
Here are my own circumstances and my own wealth. They are yours and at your disposal. Nothing of them will be kept back from you or hoarded away from you.
You are the lady of your father's community and the blessed tree from which your children spring. The merit that is yours is not to be denied,
nor are your root and your branch to be lowered. Your word is law over what my own hands possess.
But do you think I should go against your father (may God bless him and his family) in this?
She said: Glory be to God! My father, the Messenger of God, never turned away from the Book of God, nor went against its rulings.
Rather, he followed its lead and kept to its chapters.
Are you now adding to your treachery the excuse of a lie told against him?

This, after his death, is just like the deadly plots that were hatched against him during his life.

Here is the Book of God, a just judge and a decisive speaker.
It says: “…who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob” [Quran 19:6]. And it says: “And Solomon inherited from David” [Quran 27:16].

God, mighty and majestic, made matters plain in three things:
- the shares He distributed,
- the fixed portions and the laws of inheritance He laid down,

- and the portions He allowed to males and females.

This was enough to remove every excuse of the followers of falsehood, and to clear away guesswork and doubt for all who come after.
No indeed! “Rather, your own souls have made something seem fair to you. So patience is most fitting, and God is the One whose help is sought against what you describe” [Quran 12:18].

Abu Bakr said: God has spoken the truth, His Messenger has spoken the truth, and his daughter has spoken the truth. She is the mine of wisdom, the home of guidance and mercy, the pillar of the religion, and the very essence of proof. I do not dismiss what you say as wrong, nor do I reject your words.

But here are these Muslims, between you and me. They placed upon me what I now carry, and it was by their agreement that I took what I took. I did so not out of arrogance, not as a tyrant, and not to seize things for myself. They are witnesses to that.
Then Fatima (peace be upon her) turned to the women and said: O you Muslims, so quick to accept false talk, and so ready to shut your eyes to an ugly and ruinous deed!
“Do you not ponder the Quran, or are there locks upon hearts?” [Quran 47:24].
No indeed! Rather, the evil of your deeds has rusted over your hearts [echoing Quran 83:14].

It has seized your hearing and your sight.

How wretched is the interpretation you have arrived at! How evil is the course you have pointed to, and how vile the thing you have taken in exchange!
By God, you will find its load heavy and its outcome disastrous. That will be when the cover is lifted from you and the misery behind it appears.

Then there will appear to you from your Lord what you had never reckoned on, “and there and then the followers of falsehood will be the losers” [Quran 39:47; 40:78].

---
After the Sermon: At the Grave of the Messenger of God (May God Bless Him and His Family)
Then she (peace be upon her) turned toward the grave of the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said:

After you came grave tidings and tangled troubles;  
had you been here to witness them, the calamities would not have multiplied.

We have lost you as the earth loses its life-giving rain;  
your people have fallen into disorder, so witness them and do not be absent.

Would that death had come upon us before you,  
before your passing was announced and the mounds of earth came between us and you.

Men have scowled at us and treated us with contempt  
since you went from us, and every good thing they have seized.

He who took it upon himself to wrong our protector will learn,  
on the Day of Resurrection, to what end I was returning.

Men showed us what their hearts had hidden  
once you were gone, and the whole inheritance they have seized.

Every people has its kin, with closeness and rank  
before God, and the nearest of kin have the nearest claim.

We have been struck by a loss such as no grieving soul  
in all creation, Arab or non-Arab, has ever suffered.

---
Abu Bakr's Exchange with al-Zahra (Peace Be Upon Her) and Her Answer to Him
**Abu Bakr's reply:**
Abu Bakr answered her and said:

“O daughter of the Messenger of God, your father was indeed tender and generous, kind and merciful to the believers, and to the unbelievers he was a painful torment and a mighty punishment. If we trace his lineage, we find that he is your father and not the father of any other woman. He is also the brother of your cousin, and not of any other man. The Prophet preferred him over every close friend, and he aided the Prophet in every great matter. Only the blessed love you, and only the wretched hate you.

And you, best of women and daughter of the best of prophets, are truthful in what you say and foremost in the fullness of your understanding. You are not to be turned away from your right, nor barred from your truth.

“By God, I have not gone beyond the view of the Messenger of God, nor have I acted except by his leave. The scout does not lie to his own people. I call God to witness, and God is enough as a witness, that I heard the Messenger of God say: ‘We, the company of prophets, do not leave gold or silver, house or land, as inheritance. “We have assigned what you are seeking to horses and weapons. With them the Muslims will fight, wage jihad against the unbelievers, and battle the defiant evildoers. This was done by the consensus of the Muslims. I did not act on it alone, nor did I impose my own opinion.

Your word is law over what my own hands possess. So do you think I should go against your father in this?”
**The reply of Lady Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her):**
She (peace be upon her) said:

“Glory be to God! The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) never turned away from the Book of God, nor went against its rulings. Rather, he followed its lead and kept to its chapters. Are you now adding to your treachery the excuse of a lie told against him?! This, after his death, is just like the deadly plots that were hatched against him during his life!

And it says: ‘And Solomon inherited from David’ [Quran 27:16]. No indeed! ‘Rather, your own souls have made something seem fair to you. So patience is most fitting, and God is the One whose help is sought against what you describe’ [Quran 12:18].”

---
Her Conversation with the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (Peace Be Upon Him), on Her Return Home

Then she (peace be upon her) turned back toward home. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), her husband Ali, was awaiting her return and watching for her arrival. When she had settled in the house, she said to him:

“Son of Abu Talib! You have wrapped yourself up like a child in the womb, and you sit at home like a man under suspicion! You once broke the strongest feathers of the falcon, yet now the feathers of the defenceless have failed you!

“Here is the son of Abu Quhafa, wresting from me my father's gift and the bare livelihood of my two sons! He opposed me openly in my dispute, and I found him the most stubborn of adversaries in answering me. In the end, the sons of Qayla [the Helpers] withheld their support from me, and the Emigrants withheld their bond. The whole community lowered its eyes and looked away from me. No one defended me, and no one stood in the way. I went out choking back my anger, and I have come back humbled.

“You brought your own cheek low on the day you let your sharp edge go to waste! You once preyed upon wolves, and now you make the dust your bed! You have silenced no speaker, and you have been of no avail. I have no choice left. Would that I had died before this lowliness and before this humiliation!

“May God be my excuse for speaking to you so, whether I speak as one who blames you or as one who knows you as my protector! Woe is me at every sunrise! Woe is me at every sunset! The pillar has died, and the arm of support has grown weak. My complaint is to my father, and my appeal for justice is to my Lord. O God, You are mightier in strength and power, and more severe in force and in punishment.”
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to her:

“No woe is yours; woe belongs to the one who hates you. Calm your grief, daughter of the Chosen One and remnant of prophethood. I have not slackened in my religion, nor have I fallen short of what was within my power. If it is livelihood that you want, your provision is guaranteed and your Guarantor is trustworthy. What has been prepared for you is better than what has been cut off from you. So leave your reward with God.”
She (peace be upon her) said: “God is enough for me.” And she said no more.
